visual_goal: Show the level-1 capability groups with financial facts flowing into the books of record and on to close and planning, and the four overlaps flagged on Money Movement, Revenue and Billing, Close and Report, and Tax.
prompt: A left-to-right capability landscape. At the far left, five rounded boxes stacked vertically: 'Spend', 'Revenue and Billing', 'Money Movement', 'Tax', 'Treasury'. In the centre, a large open book labeled 'Record and Account'. One arrow from each of the five left boxes into the open book (five arrows). To the right of the book, a box 'Close and Report' with one arrow from the book into it, and at the far right a box 'Plan and Perform' with one arrow from 'Close and Report' into it. Above the book and 'Close and Report', a wide shield labeled 'Controls' with two dotted lines down, one to the book and one to 'Close and Report'. Below everything, a wide flat database band labeled 'Finance Data' with dotted lines up to 'Revenue and Billing', 'Money Movement' and 'Plan and Perform'. Four small red overlapping-circles warning badges, each with the word 'Overlap', are pinned on the corners of 'Revenue and Billing', 'Money Movement', 'Tax' and 'Close and Report'. Exactly seven solid arrows.
alt: Spend, revenue and billing, money movement, tax and treasury feed the books of record, which feed close and report and then plan and perform; controls assure the books and the close, finance data feeds from below, and overlap badges sit on money movement, revenue and billing, tax, and close and report.

visual_goal: Show the target context map: canonical events from brand platforms as the published language, anticorruption adapters at the PSP and ERP boundaries, and plain customer-supplier links between finance contexts.
prompt: A left-to-right context map on a light background. At the far left, a box 'Brand platforms'. In the middle on a soft teal panel: a box 'Payments' in the upper left of the panel, a box 'Subledger' in the upper right of the panel, a box 'Billing' directly below 'Subledger', and a box 'Revenue' below and to the right of 'Subledger'. From 'Brand platforms' exactly two arrows leave, each carrying a small envelope: the upper arrow ends at 'Payments'; the lower arrow runs along the top edge of the panel, passes over 'Payments' and ends at 'Subledger'. One envelope has the label 'Canonical events'. Below the far left, a small group of plain generic office buildings labeled once 'PSPs', with one arrow up into 'Payments' that passes through a small plug-adapter icon. One arrow from 'Payments' into 'Subledger', one arrow up from 'Billing' into 'Subledger', one arrow from 'Subledger' into 'Revenue'. On a soft orange panel at the right, an open book labeled 'General ledger', and at the far right a box 'Consolidation' with one arrow from the book into it. Exactly two arrows enter the book from the left, one from 'Subledger' and one from 'Revenue', and each of these two arrows passes through its own small plug-adapter icon just before the book. Exactly nine arrows and three plug-adapter icons.
alt: Brand platforms send canonical events to payments and the subledger; PSP models enter payments through an adapter; payments and billing feed the subledger, which feeds revenue; the subledger and revenue post to the general ledger through adapters, and the ledger feeds consolidation.

visual_goal: Show three overlapping capabilities traced through their applications to owning teams, with one application owned by nobody and one team owning the minority implementation of all three.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration in three horizontal rows separated by thin lines. Each row begins at the far left with a capability box, followed by a thin arrow to a short line of unlabeled application-window icons; under each window hangs a small name tag naming its owning team. Top row: box 'Account Reconciliation', then three windows tagged 'Group Close', 'No owner' and 'Wayfare'. The 'No owner' tag is an empty dashed grey tag with a question mark. Middle row: box 'Tax Determination', then two windows tagged 'Group Tax' and 'Wayfare'. Bottom row: box 'Partner Payouts', then two windows tagged 'Stayloft' and 'Wayfare'. Every 'Wayfare' tag is bright orange and the three 'Wayfare' windows line up in one vertical column on the right, inside a tall soft orange highlight band; all other tags are teal. Exactly three arrows, one per row.
alt: Account reconciliation, tax determination and partner payouts each trace to applications tagged with their owning teams: one reconciliation tool has no owner, and Wayfare owns one application in each of the three overlaps.
